name: Micronesia
headline: Micronesia is joining its state hospital records into one national system, but no law yet gives patients access, consent or privacy rights.

access.summary: Micronesia has no data protection law and no statutory right to see or copy a health record was found. The 2025 data protection bill is still pending, covers only national departments, and contains no access right.
detail: Article IV, section 5 of the Constitution protects against unreasonable search, seizure or invasion of privacy. It does not give a right to a copy of one's medical record.
Title 41 of the FSM Code (public health) has no section on patient access to records. State codes were not reviewed, so a state-level access right is not verified.

C.B. No. 24-17, the Personal Data Protection Act of 2025, was introduced on 17 May 2025. It sets data principles and a complaints process but no right of access. It applies only to core national departments and excludes purely intrastate processing, so state-run hospitals appear to fall outside it.
No patient portal was found. The Digital Health Strategic Plan talks about empowering individuals but names no portal.

control.summary: Records now sit in one national system that a clinician can open from any state, with no opt-out or patient-visible access log found. The cancer registry law requires reporting every case and only tells the patient it was reported.
detail: BES, the vendor, says the national Tamanu record lets a clinician open any patient's history from any state. No consent step, opt-out or patient access log was described.
Section 1104 of the Cancer Registry System Act requires every facility to report each cancer case to the Secretary. The patient must be informed before the report, but consent is not required.
The Digital Health Strategic Plan commits to role-based access controls and audit trails. These are plans, and no patient-facing log is mentioned.
The pending data protection bill would let national departments share personal data with each other whenever it serves a legitimate national government function and follows the bill's principles.

privacy.summary: There is no data protection law, regulator or breach notification duty, and the Health Department's own plan says sensitive patient data may be inadequately protected. A ransomware attack forced Yap's health department to take its whole network offline in March 2025.
detail: DLA Piper lists no data protection law, authority, security rule or breach notification duty in the FSM. A telecoms confidentiality duty in Title 21 covers carriers only.

The pending bill names health data as sensitive but makes the National Statistics Office its administrator, not an independent regulator. Courts may not award damages under it, and it would take effect 18 months after approval.
In March 2025 ransomware forced Yap's health department to take its whole network offline. In October 2025 the Vice President cited recent health-sector cyber incidents.
In May 2026 a Congress committee recommended against the cybercrime bill in its current form. The only health-specific penalty found is a $2,000 fine for leaking cancer registry data.

commercial.summary: No law limits the sale of health data, marketing use, data brokers or health apps. The pending data protection bill would bind only national government departments, so private clinics, insurers and app makers would stay outside it.
detail: DLA Piper finds no rules on collection, transfer or electronic marketing beyond telecommunications carriers, which may not use or disclose customer information without consent.
C.B. No. 24-17 defines data controllers as core national departments and their contractors. National state-owned entities and the FSM Insurance Board are expressly excluded.
No rule on de-identified data sales or consumer health apps was found, and no enforcement case on commercial use of health data was found.

journey.summary: The vendor BES says hospitals in Yap, Pohnpei and Kosrae now share one Tamanu record holding about 128,000 patients, with Chuuk migrating (not verified by the health department). Primary care is mostly outside it: a 2024 scan found an EHR in 4 of 119 facilities.
detail: Before the migration each state ran its own copy of a legacy EHR, so a patient's data did not follow them to another state's hospital. BES says about 128,000 patients and 530,000 encounters, back to 2018, moved into Tamanu.
Migrated data includes clinical records, procedures, labs, medications and imaging. Chuuk, the fourth state, was still underway.
A peer-reviewed scan carried out in April and May 2024 found EHRs in 4 of 119 FSM facilities (3.4%), covering all tertiary hospitals but no primary care sites.

The national plan says EHRs link partly with labs and pharmacy, but not with public health surveillance or civil registration. Immunization runs on a separate registry (FSMIIS). No link to MiCare insurance claims was found.

clinical.summary: The vendor says a clinician can open Tamanu in any of three states and see the patient's history back to 2018, but this is not verified by the health department. Chuuk was not yet migrated, and dispensaries and health centres are mostly not on it.
detail: BES reports that clinicians in Yap, Pohnpei and Kosrae work in one national Tamanu database. This comes from the vendor and was not confirmed by the health department.
The health department said in November 2025 it would begin phased Tamanu deployment in early 2026 after studying Palau's system.

The national plan says primary care data from community health centres and dispensaries is often non-standardised and outside national reporting, and many outer islands lack reliable internet or power.
No consent or emergency-access rules for clinicians viewing another state's records were found.

research.summary: Health research needs a national permit and ethics review, and cancer registry data is confidential by law with a fine or prison for misuse. There is no opt-out and no rules for research use of the new national record.
detail: The FSM research policy requires biological or medical research on people to go to the FSM Human Research Ethics Committee, with details from the health department. Whether it meets regularly was not verified.
Every researcher needs a permit from the national archives and culture office, and must obtain informants' prior informed consent and respect privacy and confidentiality.
The Cancer Registry System Act makes registry data confidential. Release to researchers needs ethics approval, and unlawful disclosure carries a $2,000 fine or six months in prison.
These safeguards cover the cancer registry and new studies. No rules on secondary use of EHR data, and no public register of uses, were found.

ai.summary: No law, guidance or device rule for clinical AI was found, and the 2022 medicines law does not cover devices. The vendor used AI to map legacy procedure and medication text to code lists, with human review.
detail: The Safe Pharmaceutical Act of 2022 regulates medicines and does not mention medical devices, so software as a medical device has no national regulator.
The Digital Health Strategic Plan 2026-2030 does not mention artificial intelligence. A June 2026 explainer by Levellers found no AI law, strategy or regulator.
BES says AI assisted in matching legacy free-text procedures and medications to standard codes during the Tamanu migration, followed by human review.
